one_month_reasoning: Events in the window. (1) EASD 2026 (Sep 28 to Oct 2) is now mostly out. ACHIEVE-4 met non-inferiority, with MACE-4 16% lower and all-cause death 57% lower in pre-planned analyses versus glargine [20]. Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 showed 20.8% weight loss in type 2 diabetes [21]. EloraTZP showed 23.3% weight loss but 10.8-27% adverse-event dropouts [23, 36]. Net: mildly positive, already partly in the price. (2) CVS Caremark returns Zepbound as co-preferred on Oct 1 for about 25-30M lives [25, 26]. That helps volume, but management has warned that net price falls as medical exceptions end. (3) Q3 results come before the open on Oct 29 [9]. Consensus is about $22.4B revenue and $9.81 EPS, below Q2's $23.0B because of the guided Q3 seasonality [1, 9]. That is a beatable bar given the Medicare uptake: 700k new seniors, 70% on Lilly drugs [22], and Foundayo scripts of about 47.5k a week, still rising [6]. The risks are a further step-down in US price, since the underlying US price fell about 9% in Q2 excluding rebate true-ups [1], and Novo's CagriSema decision, which could come in Q4 [15]. Lilly has beaten and raised in each 2026 quarter, so I tilt the median slightly up to about $1,158 (+0.7%). I use an 11% monthly sigma, wider than the 10% from 35%/sqrt(12), with a 15% weight on 15% for the earnings gap.

fair_value.method: A blend of two P/E methods. NTM EPS at the horizon of about $54.0 x 22.5x = $1,215 (weight 0.6), and CY2027 consensus EPS of $47.5 x 25.5x = $1,211 (weight 0.4). The blend is about $1,213, rounded to $1,215.

bear.story: Net price erosion speeds up. Novo's $675 list price from Jan 2027 [14], Foundayo self-pay at $149 [28], the end of CVS medical exceptions [25] and Medicare at $245 [35] cut revenue per script faster than volume grows. Foundayo stalls well below the Wegovy pill (about 172k vs 47.5k weekly) [3, 6], or CagriSema wins share. CY27 EPS is about $43 and the multiple falls to about 19-20x.

base.story: Volume beats price. CVS co-preferred status and Medicare (70% Lilly share of new seniors) keep tirzepatide on top [22, 25], Foundayo grows toward roughly $1.8B in 2027 [6], and the retatrutide BLA is filed in Q1 2027 [37]. CY27 EPS is about $47-49, and at the horizon the stock trades at about 23x NTM EPS of about $54.

bull.story: Foundayo compounds through telehealth (Hims, LillyDirect) and international launches [27], ACHIEVE-4's mortality signal helps uptake in type 2 diabetes [20], retatrutide looks best-in-class with 28% weight loss [37], and CY27 EPS beats to $52 or more. The stock re-rates to about 27.5x on about $57.5 NTM EPS, near Citi's $1,600 [33].

thesis_break_reason: Below about $840 (27% under spot, roughly 17.7x CY27 consensus and below HSBC's $940 low target [33]), the price would be signalling a fundamental break rather than ordinary volatility. Possible causes: tirzepatide net price falling faster than volume grows (the Q2 underlying US price was already -9% [1]), a safety or label problem (the MDL 3094 Rule 702 ruling going against defendants [31], or retatrutide safety in FDA review), or a policy shock that cuts CY27 EPS below about $42. Lilly's MFN deal carries a 3-year Section 232 tariff exemption [35], so tariffs are a smaller tail risk than I assumed in round 1.

reasoning: Round-1 research ran out of search budget after about 16 queries. This continuation ran about 30 more searches and fetches, mostly in my lane (alternative). Verified facts: I re-read the Q2 8-K [1]. Revenue was $23.0B (+48%), on volume +60% and worldwide realized price -13%. US price was only -3% reported and about -9% excluding rebate adjustments, so my round-1 '9-13% US price fall' overstated US erosion. Non-GAAP EPS was $8.38 after $3.03 of IPR&D, with 893.7M diluted shares. FY26 guidance is $85-87B and $35.50-36.50. New in-lane evidence. (a) Distribution: CVS restores Zepbound as co-preferred from Oct 1 [25, 26], and Hims now routes Zepbound and Foundayo to LillyDirect, with Foundayo at $149/month [27, 28]. Both widen volume and compress price. (b) Scripts: Foundayo about 47.5k a week (week to Sep 11, +8% w/w) [6] versus the Wegovy pill at about 137-172k [3, 29]. The CEO says Foundayo takes about one-third of new oral patients and that 700k seniors started GLP-1s under Medicare, 70% on Lilly drugs [22]. (c) Newsletters [23, 24] and a blog [36] flag the EloraTZP dropouts (up to 27%) as the main pipeline caveat, while retatrutide's 28.3% weight loss in TRIUMPH-1 and Q1 2027 BLA [37] underpin the long-term premium. (d) Litigation tracker: MDL 3094 has 3,848 cases, and the Rule 702 hearing was held Sep 14-18 with no settlement program [31]. That is a tail risk, not my base case. (e) Insider activity is only routine 10b5-1 sales [32]. Short interest is 0.8% of float [6]. (f) Prediction markets: the only Lilly market I found is a resolved earnings-call wording market on Polymarket ($12.2K volume) [30], so I have no usable probability. X was not fetched directly. (g) Tariffs: Lilly's MFN deal gives a 3-year Section 232 exemption [35]. Sell-side context: the average target is about $1,292-1,325, with a range of $850/940 to $1,600 [33]; I treat it as evidence only. Valuation: blended P/E fair value of $1,215 (from $1,195), on a slightly higher forward multiple because US price erosion is milder than I thought and EASD de-risked the pipeline. Scenarios: $850 / $1,240 / $1,580 at 25/50/25, a mean of about $1,228. Ladder: a lognormal with median $1,205 and an 80/20 mixture of 31% and 45% sigma. 31% is a little under the 35% realized vol because last year included one-off trial and policy shocks; the 45% component fattens the tails for price and policy shocks. P(>= spot) is about 0.56.
